summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record Rs 141.8 crore (+85% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 29.4%, helped by the Indonesia transfer-case order.
summary.overview: Revenue of Rs 141.8 crore rose 85% YoY and 25% QoQ, with transfer cases up 93% YoY to Rs 76 crore. EBITDA was Rs 41.6 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT was Rs 25.2 crore (17.8% margin). Management framed the quarter as the start of a broader growth phase, citing the Indonesia programme, exports, components, and a planned US greenfield plant (Project Mayflower). EV transmission deliveries were soft in Q1 and management expects a pickup in schedules over the next three quarters.

segments.name: Transfer case
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 76 crore, +93% YoY, ~53% of total; driven by Indonesia programme volumes and existing OEM platforms. Management said ~30% of the ~70,000-unit Indonesia contract has been dispatched.

segments.name: E-gear drive (EV transmission)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5.7 crore; described as subdued in Q1 as a Tata localisation programme slowed. Management says quarterly run-rate expectation rises from Rs 6.5-7 crore to Rs 10-12 crore.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 34.4 crore, +83% YoY, helped by improved realisations, higher precision-component mix and export growth.

segments.name: Other (NexTrac, ALH, Synchro, aftermarket, other income)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 21.4 crore vs Rs 6.5 crore in Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Management expects further transfer case momentum through FY27 from pickup truck, new platform and facelift programmes; ~50% of Indonesia business described as potentially recurring.
Management said some Indonesia volume may spill into the first 1-2 months of next year because of supply chain constraints.

EV transmission schedules expected to rise to Rs 10-12 crore per quarter, with management saying tactically this should hold for the next three quarters; Tata PPAP approval received, awaiting Tata testing.
US greenfield plant in Greenville, South Carolina: second half CY28 at the earliest; initial investment directionally ~$5 million.
Automatic transmission programmes expected to start second half FY/CY28 (management used both framings); minimum Rs 300-400 crore business potential.
Manual LCV transmission beachhead contract expected to start revenue next year; India opportunity Rs 100-150 crore and above.
Management targets first Rs 1,000 crore revenue milestone before Rs 2,000 crore; sustainable EBITDA target of 20-22% and above, with ROIC of at least 18% as a benchmark.
capex_capacity: Two existing transfer-case assembly lines (over 20 years old) are being modernised with a German automation partner; the new line is expected to deliver ~400 units/day or ~120,000 units/year at the Shirwal facility.
Land holdings: 25 acres at Sirsi, Karnataka and 10 acres at Shirwal; management says capacity is not currently a constraint.
US: wholly-owned subsidiary set up in Greenville, SC at the International Center for Automotive Research; greenfield plant planned, initial investment directionally ~$5 million.
Management said investment in India will be larger than overseas investment and will take priority.
demand_pricing: Indonesia programme: ~70,000 transfer cases for Tata and Mahindra over 10-12 months; competitors included Toyota, Nissan, Mitsubishi, Isuzu, Great Wall and Foton. Management said the tender saved the Indonesian government ~$500 million.
Principal customer is Mahindra; Tata Motors is number two. Divgi says its export contracts are exclusive, with it as the only supplier of these components into North America.
Global transfer case market cited at ~14-15 million units (management), with a separate analyst figure of 40-50 million that management did not confirm.
Management says FWD-based AWD content can exceed Rs 30,000 per vehicle; two new applications added in the last 4-6 months.
Indian EV transmission market is crowded; Tata is the main localisation leader and Divgi's primary transmission supplier. Korean EV opportunity in discussion.
Management expects exports and global operations to be 25-40% of business and domestic 60-70%, with proprietary products becoming a larger share of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What investment is needed for the US facility, and what capital and factory requirements look ahead over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial phase directionally about $5 million for a small compact facility near Greenville, SC, close to BorgWarner's plant; the US local-content mandate makes a local plant necessary to qualify. Management said Indian investment will be larger than overseas and takes primacy.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-top customer domestic transfer case traction, and export revenue plus Indonesia order progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahindra is the principal customer and Tata Motors is number two. Exports were about Rs 23 crore in Q1 and about Rs 34 crore cumulative, annualising to about Rs 92 crore; the Indonesia order is treated as export in substance but not booked as export.

qa_highlights.question: Which other OEMs are adopting 4x4 or AWD transfer cases, and how durable is 4WD demand in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Prototype or development work is underway with Force Motors, Eicher, Ashok Leyland, Tata and Mahindra. Management says 4WD demand will persist in commercial trucks and off-road uses, and that the indirect export channel will be larger than domestic demand.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for next transfer case, manual and automatic transmission orders and revenue starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipments to South Africa are expected from April 2028 to March 2029, which management says is the same as the global pickup truck contract. A manual LCV beachhead contract (India opportunity Rs 100-150 crore and above) starts earning revenue next year. Automatic transmission earliest in 2H FY28/CY28, with Rs 300-400 crore minimum potential.

qa_highlights.question: How many Indonesia transfer cases were dispatched, and what is the EV dispatch run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of the roughly 70,000-unit contract is dispatched, with spillover of 1-2 months into next year possible. EV schedules were Rs 6.5-7 crore a quarter on average, now forecast at Rs 10-12 crore; Tata PPAP approval received, with Tata vehicle testing pending.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28-FY29 reach the Rs 2,000 crore goal early, and can margins be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 1,000 crore is the first milestone, with four or five chunks of Rs 150-400 crore needed. It guarded margin expectations: it sustained about 20% EBITDA even in FY26 when annual revenue was about Rs 240 crore, and targets 20-22% and above, with ROIC of at least 18% as a benchmark.

risks_watch: Indonesia execution: about 30% of ~70,000 units dispatched; some volume may spill into the first 1-2 months of next year, and OEM capacity and supply-chain constraints are cited as drivers.
Revenue concentration: Mahindra is the principal customer and Tata Motors is number two; Tata is also the main EV localisation customer.
EV transmission timing: the Tata programme slowed on vehicle testing; PPAP is in hand, but the Rs 10-12 crore quarterly run-rate depends on Tata testing and on market holding over three quarters.
US plant: greenfield at 2H CY28 at the earliest, initial investment directionally ~$5 million; the project is still at RFQ stage and conversion to awards is pending.
Margin sustainability: management said Q1's 29.4% EBITDA reflects a one-off opportunity and guided to 20-22%; the range of outcomes is wide.
Automatic transmission and new programmes (2H FY28 start, Rs 300-400 crore minimum) remain unproven; the Korean EV order is in discussion only; management flagged execution bandwidth as a constraint.
key_quotes: And we believe that this quarter marks the beginning of a new phase of our corporate journey since 2023 when we went public.
So, I think four-wheel drive cannot be wished away because the commercial truck market will continue to be diesel.
But because of their impediments in the rest of the supply chain and all that, some of this contract may spill over into the one or two months of the next year.
So, the first order of business is to cross that 1,000.
The reality is that the investments within India will definitely be more than overseas.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and expansive on the growth pipeline, US plant, and automatic transmission, but cautious on near-term EV timing and on the Indonesia run-rate. It was evasive on the exact automatic transmission timeline and product architecture, citing competitive sensitivity, and gave directional rather than firm numbers on the Rs 2,000 crore target.

adds.what: Modernised transfer-case assembly line (replacing one of two 20+ year old lines) at Shirwal, ~400 units/day or ~120,000 units/yr
US greenfield plant in Greenville, South Carolina (initial investment ~$5 million)

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 141.8 cr (+85% YoY) is backed by the Indonesia order (~30% of ~70,000 units dispatched) and EV schedules guided up to Rs 10-12 cr/qtr, but no explicit FY27 revenue growth guidance was given, the new 120k/yr line timing is undated, and the US plant is only CY28 at the earliest.
